text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat discuss the developments in the peace process and the situation in the occupied territories. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said contacts were continuing between the Palestinian and Israeli sides on confidence building, settlements and other issues.
- A Jordanian and Egyptian committee will hold talks in Cairo on Saturday to discuss ways of increasing bilateral trade to 300 million pounds a year.

- Public prosecutor agrees to send to court 23 leaders of the Gama'a Islamiya group accused of organising explosions and assassinations targeting individuals, police, artists, journalists and foreign tourists.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily issues a decision to halt the importation of beef from Belgium after the European Commission said that 1,600 tonnes of British beef had been exported illegally, with Belgian help, despite a ban because of the mad cow crisis, and also because of the possibility that 900 tonnes had been exported to Egypt and Russia.
- 100 million pounds in loans from agricultural banks has been set aside for farmers to help them buy land, in response to the new land law which ends the perpetuated rental relationship.
- Mubarak's calls to set up a common market will be discussed by the Jordanian-Egyptian committee on Saturday.
